sn47.2:1.1: At one time the Buddha was staying near Vesālī, in Ambapālī’s mango grove.
sn47.2:1.2: There the Buddha addressed the bhikkhus,
sn47.2:2.1: “Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu should live with awareness and comprehension.
sn47.2:2.2: This is my instruction to you.
sn47.2:2.3: And how is a bhikkhu aware?
sn47.2:2.4: It’s when a bhikkhu meditates by observing an aspect of the body—ardently aware and comprehending, without craving and aversion towards the world
sn47.2:2.5: They meditate observing an aspect of feelings …
sn47.2:2.7: principles—ardently aware and comprehending, without craving and aversion towards the world
sn47.2:2.8: That’s how a bhikkhu is aware.
sn47.2:3.1: And how is a bhikkhu comprehending?
sn47.2:3.2: It’s when a bhikkhu acts with comprehension when going out and coming back; when looking ahead and aside; when bending and extending the limbs; when bearing the outer robe, bowl and robes; when eating, drinking, chewing, and tasting; when urinating and defecating; when walking, standing, sitting, sleeping, waking, speaking, and keeping silent.
sn47.2:3.3: That’s how a bhikkhu acts with comprehension.
sn47.2:3.4: A bhikkhu should live with awareness and comprehension.
sn47.2:3.5: This is my instruction to you.”
